statement: Desired replication factor has a policy authority that is independent of replica identities: it comes only from a valid persisted policy row for the owning table, creation initializes that policy from the owning table's schema declaration, runtime identity mutation cannot change a declared policy, and an identity count is never persisted as desired RF. A minted replace-replica-<hex> is a new identity, not a changed factor. This Quest establishes the substrate ONLY; it does not claim that every behaviour-changing consumer already resolves through it.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Exactly one module decodes a persisted policy row into a desired replication factor, returning a frozen {replicationFactor, source} projection and nothing else; it mints no runtime state, reads only own data properties, never executes an accessor on a candidate row, and rejects arrays, inherited values, non-integers, coercible strings and non-positive values as UNDECLARED with factor 0.

The creation default for each table is READ from that table's own schema declaration, so PARTITIONS rows follow the PARTITIONS declaration and MESSAGE_GROUPS rows follow the MESSAGE_GROUPS declaration; the schema default seeds a NEW row and is never used to reinterpret a row that failed to declare a usable value.

No code path derives, writes, or persists a desired replication factor from a replica identity list: getInitialReplicaIds hands out a copy, PartitionService and MessageGroupService copy the peer list they are given, seed hand-offs do not alias the declaration, and no identity count such as replicas.length is written into a policy field.

This Quest proves the substrate only. It makes NO claim that every behaviour-changing desired-RF consumer resolves through the authority, states no consumer inventory, and does not repair the known move-planner table-policy fallback; those belong to the successor quest behaviour-changing-consumer-convergence and to S6.

Proof is a deterministic raw node:test witness with one anchored scenario per receipt, red on HEAD and green after, with a from-scratch mutation matrix in which every mutation of the substrate reds at least one named receipt.
